faq.q1.q: How does the AI choose recommendations?
faq.q1.a: A four-layer pipeline: SKU-tag × event overlap → category fallback → KNN over embeddings (768-d, COSINE) → boost from AI memory (what the farmer accepted before). No magic — every decision is explained by four numbers, and they show up right on the card.
faq.q2.a: SKU catalogs never leave your instance. Gemini sees only canonical text ("apple honey 250 g, meadow apiary, Moscow region") — no prices, no stock, no buyer names. SurrealDB lives on your server, embeddings stay local.
faq.q3.q: Where do events and trends come from?
faq.q3.a: 40+ events curated by hand: public, Orthodox, seasonal, themed. Trends are pulled from YAML seeds and extend without a restart. Every event has a prep window, target channels, and an influence weight on the recommender.
faq.q4.a: Every AI output is a draft. Edit the text by hand, save as a new version (revision history is built in), publish or archive. The AI is a starting point, never the final word. The team stays in the loop through the activity log on each plan card.
faq.q5.q: How does generation for social, blogs and stories work?
faq.q5.a: One content engine, five channels — each with its own prompt and body shape: stories, blogs, recipes, social, push. Each gets its own editor and preview — editorial layout for the blog, IG-tile with carousel, lock-screen mock for push.
faq.q6.q: How do recommendations adapt to the season?
faq.q6.a: 12 seasonal windows and 5 trends live in the graph as influence edges (`influences`, `covers`). When building the calendar, the recommender reads active windows and applies a boost to matching events. Season ends — boost lifts, no manual edits.
faq.q7.q: Does this work for small farms and local markets?
faq.q7.a: Yes — and that's the primary case. For a small farmer with 24 SKUs the system delivers what major brands need a full marketing team for: calendar, content, channels, ROI. Architecturally multi-tenant; locally just one docker-compose up and the service is live.
